reason: Under Throughput Optimized HDD volumes, the quote states that on sizes 0.125 TiB to 16 TiB baseline throughput varies from 5 MiB/s to a cap of 500 MiB/s, reached at 12.5 TiB.
Under the st1 throughput credits heading, the quote states burst throughput varies from 31 MiB/s to a cap of 500 MiB/s, reached at 2 TiB.

The quotes support st1 as a low cost HDD volume for frequently accessed, throughput-intensive workloads, but no quote states that sc1 is the choice for infrequently accessed data; the second quote only says st1, though similar to sc1, supports frequently accessed data.
In the st1 credits section, the quote states throughput is capped at a maximum of 500 MiB/s and after the bucket is depleted it is limited to the baseline rate of 40 MiB/s per TiB.
Under Example 5 (st1) on the pricing page, the quote uses a region that charges $0.045 per GB-month; the claim and condition mark it as an example Region rate.
The st1 value line lists Use Cases: Big data, data warehouses, log processing, and the user guide quote says st1 fits large, sequential workloads such as Amazon EMR and ETL.

The quote states both branches exactly: st1 for scans up to 500 MiB/s or several full scans a day; sc1 when optimizing for cost, data relatively infrequently accessed and not needing more than 250 MiB/s.

The first quote states the default disables I/O on potential inconsistency and the status becomes impaired; the second states you can override the default by configuring the volume to automatically enable I/O (the Auto-Enable IO attribute in context).
The quote states the completion duration is between 15 minutes and 48 hours and must be specified in 15 minute increments, for time-based snapshot and EBS-backed AMI copies.
The quote states copies within and across AWS Regions complete in a specified timeframe and help meet stringent disaster recovery requirements (RPO and RTO).
Under Pricing and billing, the quotes state quota-caused misses are billed on the actual completion duration, and service-side failure or cancellation means no additional charges.
The quota table row states the maximum throughput of a single time-based snapshot copy operation is 500 MiB/s, Adjustable No, applying per snapshot for AMI copies.
The quotes state charges are per GiB copied at a rate based on requested duration, and the example bills $30 ($0.010 x 3,000 GiB) for an 8-hour duration.
The quote states additional charges apply, at a rate based on the requested completion duration, per GiB of snapshot data copied.
The quote states an EBS volume is a durable, block-level storage device you attach to instances and then use as you would use a physical hard drive.
Under Data persistence, the quotes state you pay for volume usage as long as the data persists and the data persists until the volume is deleted explicitly.

The quotes state volume copies are created immediately, copied volumes can be accessed instantly without waiting for the data, and copy operations don't affect source volume performance; context gives the baseline-during-initialization condition.
The quote states the copy operation is charged based on the size of data blocks written to the source volume at copy creation and the new volume is charged like any other EBS volume.
The quotes state a volume copy is a crash-consistent, point-in-time copy and must be created in the same Availability Zone as the source volume.
The quotes state a volume from a snapshot begins as an exact replica of the source volume, and a created volume can be attached to any EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone.
The quote states that omitting --size uses the source snapshot's volume size and a specified size must be equal to or larger than it.
The quotes state blocks must be downloaded from Amazon S3 to a volume created from a snapshot and during initialization the volume might experience increased I/O latency and decreased performance.

The quotes support an optional rate from 100 to 300 MiB/s that makes volumes fully performant in a predictable time, but the qualifier condition that specifying a rate incurs additional charges is not in the quotes or their context.
The quotes state EBS volumes persist independently from the running life of an EC2 instance and an EBS volume is off-instance storage.
The quotes state EBS volumes are presented as raw, unformatted block devices and you format the volume with a file system such as Ext4 or NTFS and then install applications.
The quote states a new EBS volume is automatically replicated within its Availability Zone to prevent data loss due to failure of any single hardware component.
The quote states you can attach multiple EBS volumes to a single instance and the volume and instance must be in the same Availability Zone.
Under Elastic Volumes Limitations, the quote states you can't decrease the volume size but can create a smaller volume and migrate data with rsync or robocopy.
The quote states you can stop and restart an EBS-backed instance without affecting data in the attached volume, which remains attached throughout the stop-start cycle.
The quote lists exactly gp2 and gp3, io1 and io2, st1, sc1 and Magnetic (standard) with the same family names.

The quotes state each EBS volume is replicated within its Availability Zone, EFS is a regional service storing data within and across multiple AZs, and EFS provides shared access to thousands of EC2 instances.
On the EC2 storage options page, the quotes state an EBS volume persists independently with snapshots stored in Amazon S3, and instance store data is lost on stop, hibernate or terminate.
In REL09-BP01 implementation guidance, the quotes state Amazon EBS has built in backup capabilities and AWS Backup centralizes and automates data protection across AWS services.
In SEC08-BP02, the quotes say to encrypt private data at rest and give the EC2 example of default encryption on accounts so new EBS volumes are automatically encrypted.
Under Xen-based Linux instances, the quote states more than 40 volumes can cause boot failures and the count includes root, instance store and EBS volumes; context gives the best-effort note.
The quote states instance store volumes can be attached only at launch and can't be attached after launch.
The quote states stopping an instance erases data on any instance store volumes and data you need should be copied to persistent storage such as Amazon EBS or Amazon S3 first.
The table row under the event header states that when the underlying disk fails, the data on the failed disk does not persist.
The footnote on the instance store data persistence page states the data is not included in the EBS-backed AMI nor on instance store volumes of instances launched from that AMI.
The quote states data persists through reboot but not stop, hibernate or terminate, when every block of the instance store volume is cryptographically erased.
